_comment: The SRD races, written as EFFECTS rather than as prose.
An effect names what it touches, what kind of bonus it is, and how much -
and the engine then applies 3.5's stacking rules to it along with every
other effect on the character. So a dwarf's +2 Appraise on stonework and a
homebrew race's +2 Appraise are handled by the same code, and a player's
own content is a first-class citizen rather than a note in a text box.
An effect carrying a `condition` is never added to a total: nothing here
can know whether you are fighting a giant. Those are listed on the sheet
beside the number they would modify, which is what a paper sheet does too.
See web/engine/effects.js for the vocabulary of targets and bonus types.

races.name: Human

effects.note: 4 extra skill points at 1st level, 1 per level after

races.traits: Bonus feat at 1st level. Four extra skill points at 1st level and one per level after. Favored class: any.

races.name: Dwarf
races.traits: Darkvision 60 ft. Stonecunning. Stability: +4 against bull rush and trip while standing on the ground. Weapon familiarity: dwarven waraxe and urgrosh. Speed 20 ft, never reduced by armor or load.

races.name: Elf
races.traits: Immune to magic sleep effects. Low-light vision. Proficient with longsword, rapier, longbow and shortbow. Notices a secret door on passing within 5 ft, with a Search check.

races.name: Gnome
races.traits: Low-light vision. Weapon familiarity: gnome hooked hammer. Illusions you cast have a save DC 1 higher. Speak with animals 1/day, and dancing lights, ghost sound and prestidigitation 1/day with Charisma 10 or better.

races.name: Half-Elf
races.traits: Immune to magic sleep effects. Low-light vision. Elven blood: counts as an elf for anything that cares.

races.name: Half-Orc
races.traits: Darkvision 60 ft. Orc blood: counts as an orc for anything that cares.

races.name: Halfling
races.traits: +1 on all saving throws, and a further +2 morale bonus against fear. Weapon familiarity: halflings treat the sling as a simple weapon in every way that matters to them.
